ov: A blue-grey billfish of the open ocean, named for the huge dorsal fin that runs almost the whole length of its back. It grows fast, reaching 1.2–1.5 m in its first year, and hunts schools of small fish by slashing and tapping them with its bill.

why.dg: Usually no threat, but sailfish have attacked in self-defence: one stabbed a woman with its bill when her party tried to catch it.
why.et: A hard-fighting game fish, but less valued than marlin and usually released.

rg: Open water in all the world's oceans.
df: Small schooling fish and squid, near the surface or at middle depths.
fx: Only about 24% of its attacks catch a fish, but the injured fish are easier for the next sailfish.
It may change colour to confuse prey or signal to other sailfish.
